abstract.role: Broad unstructured summary for a multidisciplinary Nature Portfolio reader.
include: one-sentence clinical or scientific context
clear study objective
high-level cohort and evaluation setting only when needed for credibility
main evidence-backed findings and their implication
abstract.pathology_ai_emphasis: State why the pathology problem matters before naming the model; keep technical detail subordinate to the finding.

introduction.role: Clinical and scientific context that narrows to the study objective.
include: disease or pathology workflow burden
why digital pathology or computational pathology is relevant
what current approaches cannot yet resolve
study gap stated in clinical/scientific terms
final paragraph with objective, hypothesis, and what is evaluated
introduction.pathology_ai_emphasis: Use citations selectively to frame need, validation gap, and generalizability; do not create a separate Related Work section.

results.role: Self-contained discovery narrative placed before Methods.
include: brief study design and cohort/task context before first finding
figure- and table-led subsections in logical order
primary performance with n, confidence intervals, and locked metrics
secondary analyses such as external validation, subgroup robustness, ablation, calibration, or interpretability when available
failure modes or boundary conditions when supported by evidence
avoid: method recipes better suited for Methods
unsupported comparisons to state of the art
raw metric values not grounded in evidence
results.pathology_ai_emphasis: Each subsection should start with the biological or clinical question, then report the finding, then point to the relevant figure or table.

discussion.role: Interpret findings, limitations, and generalizability without new results.
include: principal findings in plain scientific language
relationship to prior pathology and AI work
clinical or biological interpretation
limitations in cohort composition, labels, scanners, staining, sites, and retrospective design
generalizability and deployment caveats
future validation or reproducibility needs
avoid: claims of clinical readiness without external/prospective evidence
discussion.pathology_ai_emphasis: Separate what the evidence supports from what remains a translational hypothesis.

include: cohort sources, inclusion/exclusion criteria, slide preparation, scanner/stain details, and ethics when available
data splits, leakage controls, labels, annotation process, and pathologist review protocol
model architecture or algorithm, preprocessing, training, hyperparameters, and inference procedure
evaluation metrics, statistical tests, confidence intervals, sample sizes, and comparison protocol
external validation or subgroup analysis definitions
software, compute environment, random seeds, code availability, data availability, and LLM-assisted writing disclosure when relevant
avoid: headline claims without enough procedural detail
private paths, case identifiers, institutions, or PHI
moving result interpretation out of Results/Discussion
omitting reproducibility information for central code
methods.pathology_ai_emphasis: Make cohort/model/evaluation choices auditable enough for another pathology AI group to reproduce the analysis.

narrative_principles.primary_reader: scientifically broad reader with biomedical/pathology interest, not only ML reviewers
narrative_principles.preferred_flow: clinical context -> objective -> findings -> interpretation -> detailed reproducibility
narrative_principles.citation_style: citations in Introduction and Discussion; no citations in Abstract; Results cite only when needed for dataset or comparator context
narrative_principles.locked_evidence_policy: metrics, figure/table references, and cohort facts must come from PathLab locked evidence and public artifacts

abstract.purpose: Summarize the study for a broad Scientific Reports readership before the main text.
must_include: broad scientific or clinical context
study objective
brief method and evidence source
strongest supported finding through metric placeholders when useful
careful implication and scope
abstract.citation_policy: Do not use citations in the abstract.
abstract.metrics_policy: Use metric placeholders for all numeric findings; keep numbers sparse.
abstract.figures_tables_policy: Do not include figures or tables.
abstract.tone: Accessible, declarative, and cautious rather than conference-pitch style.

introduction.purpose: Establish scientific context, knowledge gap, and study objective.
must_include: clinical/scientific motivation for WSI analysis
limitations of existing automation or validation practice
why evidence-locked reporting matters for reproducibility
clear statement of the study aim
brief description of what was evaluated
introduction.citation_policy: Use selected references for background and required citations from the literature draft.
introduction.metrics_policy: Do not preview detailed metric values.
introduction.figures_tables_policy: Avoid figures unless a ready overview figure is central to comprehension.

results.purpose: Present findings before Methods in a self-contained Scientific Reports style.
must_include: main empirical finding from locked results
dataset/evaluation context sufficient to understand the finding
primary table and all ready figures
external validation, calibration, or ablation findings only when locked
explicit distinction between observed findings and interpretation
results.citation_policy: Use few citations; Results should primarily report this study's evidence.
results.metrics_policy: All numeric findings must use metric placeholders; do not type raw values.
results.figures_tables_policy: Include every ready manifest figure with its figure_id and path; tables must come only from table_paths.
results.tone: Self-contained, factual, and readable for non-method specialists.

discussion.purpose: Interpret the study findings, limitations, and implications after Results.
must_include: summary of principal findings without restating every number
interpretation relative to reproducibility and validation needs
limitations tied to cohort scope, evidence gaps, or missing external validation
practical implications stated cautiously
future work based on evidence gaps
discussion.citation_policy: Use selected citations to contextualize findings with prior work.
discussion.metrics_policy: Prefer qualitative references to Results; use placeholders only if repeating a key result is necessary.
discussion.figures_tables_policy: Do not introduce new figures or tables unless already ready and not better placed in Results.

methods.purpose: Provide detailed reproducibility information after Discussion, following Scientific Reports conventions.
methods.recommended_length: Detailed enough for reproduction; can be longer than MICCAI methods.
must_include: cohort/data source description from locked evidence
model architecture, preprocessing, and training/inference details from locked blocks
evaluation metrics, split protocol, and statistical procedures when available
privacy scrubbing and provenance controls
software/reproducibility details only if present in evidence
methods.citation_policy: Cite method and evaluation references where selected.
methods.metrics_policy: Do not report outcome values; describe metric definitions and procedures.
methods.figures_tables_policy: Dataset or protocol tables may appear if table_paths provide them.
must_avoid: conference-style compression that hides reproducibility details

experiments.purpose: If retained as a separate section, act as an evaluation-protocol bridge rather than a second Results section.
must_include: evaluation design and task roles
dataset/split facts from locked evidence
baseline, ablation, and external-validation availability
metric definitions without values
experiments.citation_policy: Use citations only for standard protocols or baselines.
experiments.metrics_policy: Name metrics but do not report values.
experiments.figures_tables_policy: Prefer tables from table_paths; avoid new figures unless ready.

related_work.purpose: Provide concise prior-work context if the selected template keeps a separate Related Work section.
must_include: relevant WSI/MIL literature
clinical validation or reproducibility literature
brief comparison to the present evidence-locked study
related_work.citation_policy: Use selected references and required citations; avoid unverified claims about prior work.
related_work.metrics_policy: Do not present numeric prior-work comparisons unless locked evidence supports them.
related_work.tone: Background-like and concise, because Scientific Reports often integrates related work into the Introduction.

conclusion.purpose: End with the study's evidence-supported implication.
must_include: principal supported finding
evidence-locked reporting contribution
careful implication for future validation
